clue.text: Sailors following course they may traverse quickly

indicators.note: following puts the sailors after the course, so they come second in the answer

parts.note: Epsom is the racecourse in Surrey where the Derby is run
salts is an old word for seasoned sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors trailing behind on a course they hope to cross at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a Surrey racecourse. The definition is a wry one: the salts are a laxative, so they pass through the body quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are a purgative that passes rapidly through the gut, a humorous description of the laxative.

clue.text: Finish with title taken by the Spanish

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A title won by Spain at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy coating, a surface finish on paint or metal.

clue.text: Nameless transgressor covering up hard evidence of fight

nameless says the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: a sinner transgresses moral law

explanation.surface: An unnamed wrongdoer hides firm proof of a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' removes N from SINNER, giving SINER, which 'covering up' wraps round H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner is a black eye, the bruise left by a punch.

clue.text: Turn of card forecast slip-up

indicators.note: turn of says the card word is turned round

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone
a calculation is an estimate or forecast

explanation.surface: Predicting the next card dealt, then making an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of' reverses SIM, the card in a mobile phone, to give MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscalculation is an error of judgement, a mistake or blunder.

clue.text: A County Council garden getting church approval

explanation.definitionFit: Accedence is the act of agreeing or consenting, a form of assent.

clue.text: Symbol some came to tolerate in hindsight

explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or emblem venerated as a symbol of a group.

clue.text: Square retro hairstyle cut short

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the hairstyle word is turned round

parts.note: a bun is a hairstyle with the hair coiled at the back

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned square haircut trimmed short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns BUN into NUB. The whole clue reads like a description of a haircut, but 'cut short' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff them abruptly, cutting them off without ceremony.

clue.text: Wedding ceremony — groom plans it around mid-January

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters surround another piece

mid- says the middle letter of the month is taken

explanation.surface: A groom plans the wedding for mid-January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' rearranges PLANS IT, and 'around' puts that round U, the middle of January.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials are the formal marriage rites, a wedding.

clue.text: Dreadful bind, getting a taste for illegal activity

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly done, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
to try is to taste or sample

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges BIND with A to give BANDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by armed outlaws, lawless criminal conduct.

clue.text: Beatle hero Ringo's 'gear' — swinging!

indicators.note: swinging means moving to and fro, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Beatle praising Ringo's fashionable clothes in the Swinging Sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' was 1960s slang for great, and Swinging London fits the period.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was the lead guitarist of the Beatles.

clue.text: One getting into difficulties later!

the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.definitionFit: Spanish farewell, used like 'see you later!' as an informal parting word.

clue.text: Engineer protecting missing good vintage cycle part

missing says a letter is left out of the word before it

explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes G from PROTECTING, leaving PROTECTIN, which 'Engineer' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotter pin is a tapered fastening that held cranks onto the axle of older bicycles.

clue.text: Given time and light initially stormy Med becomes green

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so these letters are tossed about

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: initially says just the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough Mediterranean, given time and some light, turns green.
explanation.walkthrough: ERA plus L (the start of 'light') and MED are thrown together by 'stormy' to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a vivid shade of green, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Short skirts are archaic, that's it!

art is the old form of are, as in 'thou art'

explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it; Martini is a brand of that vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Martini is a famous brand of Italian vermouth, the drink called 'It' in gin and It.

clue.text: Knockabout Lee Evans recast with dismissal of a very minor character who catches the eye

with dismissal of says some letters are sent away from the name

the Roman numeral I is 1

explanation.surface: A gloomy first act staged in a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means dour and sullen, from the supposed influence of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: 'East London Eye' is epic Emin creation

explanation.surface: A new work by Tracey Emin depicting the London Eye.

explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang uses mince pie for eye, so it is an East End word for eye.

clue.text: Selection from orchestra — it engenders distress

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Borneo's overthrown king

clue.text: Plain sailing primarily with Bolt closing on back-to-back records

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

clue.text: All over the place it's trendy to eat ragout regularly

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the word is taken

taken as written
